title: fix(metadata-protocol)!: refuse publishing a hierarchy-scope grant when no hierarchy resolver is mounted; explain names the absent resolver (#26188)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X35pgvocjuh1o5vbpJ4ZCyZ)_

Fixes #26188

Clause-②: yes (narrowing: on a runtime with no hierarchy resolver, publishing a permission set whose grant uses `own_and_reports`, `unit` or `unit_and_below` is refused, where it used to answer 200; widened: `@objectstack/spec/security` gains the export `findHierarchyScopeGrants`, and `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s `ExplainEngineDeps` gains the optional member `hierarchyResolverMounted`)
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: #26059 ruling Q3 / Q4 (`6416233738`), items 9a and 9b of the item reading (`6415971852`); routes agreed with the server seat before the claim (claim `6424008328`)

## Summary

Hierarchy depths (`own_and_reports`, `unit`, `unit_and_below`) are enforced only by the enterprise hierarchy resolver (capability `hierarchy-security`, ADR-0057). Without one, the open sharing service evaluates them as `own`. `defineStack` already refuses such a grant at authoring time. A runtime save of the same permission set used to answer 200 with no word, though, and explain then blamed the caller's unit.

**9a, the save and publish doors.**

- **Rule location.** The check is a gate-local rule in the runtime authoring gate (`runtime-authoring-gate.ts`), beside the #6285 and #21476 rules. Its input is a deployment fact, so `AUTHORING_RULES` must not judge it.
  - Resolver presence is a host fact. `protocol.hierarchyResolverMounted()` reads the kernel service `hierarchy-scope-resolver` on every write, the same lookup the sharing plugin uses, and `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` passes it in. This is the shape `rlsMembershipResolverKeys` has. It does not detect the resolver by plugin name.
  - A host with no service registry (the CLI) states nothing, and nothing is judged there. `defineStack` is that host's door.
- **Publish, resolver absent.** These all answer 422 `INVALID_METADATA` with one `issues[]` entry per grant, under the rule `hierarchy-scope-capability-required`:
  - a direct active save;
  - the per-item publish of a draft;
  - the package batch publish;
  - a restore to such a version.

  Each entry is located at `permissions.NAME.objects.OBJECT.readScope` (or `writeScope`), and its message names `hierarchy-security`.
- **Draft save, resolver absent.** The save answers 200. `advisories` carries the same entry at `severity: 'warning'`.
  - D1 still holds: no rule gates a draft. The draft branch reads no collection, so a draft pays nothing new.
  - The UI already renders `advisories` as a "Saved, with warnings" toast.
- **Resolver mounted.** Nothing changes on either door.
- **Shared list and sentence.** `@objectstack/spec/security` exports `findHierarchyScopeGrants`, the one list of hierarchy depths and the one finding sentence. `validateHierarchyScopeCapability` now reads it, and `defineStack`'s refusal text is byte-identical to before (`stack-refusal-envelopes.test.ts` holds).

**Why the code is `INVALID_METADATA`, not `STACK_HIERARCHY_SCOPE_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED`.**

- The runtime authoring gate refuses with one envelope: 422 `INVALID_METADATA`, with `issues[].rule`. Every gate-local refusal (#6285, #20312) rides that envelope rather than adding a second envelope or a second throw site. A rule inside it reaches all four write doors above at once.
- Stamping the `STACK_*` code at an HTTP door would need a provenance row under `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` in `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, a file this claim keeps off (sibling #26189). That ledger row also reads `door: 'none'`, `defineStack` only.
- `INVALID_METADATA` is already registered for this package, so no ledger row is added. The server seat agreed this route before the claim.

**9b, explain.**

- **The new branch.** `explain-engine.ts`'s depth-layer record cell gains a resolver-absent branch, just ahead of the arm the card names as misleading (`sharingMatches === false`). It reads: "Hierarchy resolver absent — requires enterprise; depth evaluated as 'own'." The outcome is `excluded` when the owner-match failed, and `not_evaluated` when a share admitted the row.
- **Placement.** The branch sits after the "depth admitted this row" arm. So a row the depth really admitted is never reported as resolver-absent.
- **The dependency.** `ExplainEngineDeps.hierarchyResolverMounted` is optional, and absent means the cell reads as before. `security-plugin-explain-access.ts` wires it from `resolveKernelService('hierarchy-scope-resolver')`.

## Tests

Head `1267e3cb` (main merged at `617f27eb`).

- `runtime-authoring-gate.hierarchy-scope.test.ts` (new, pure gate, 7 tests):
  - publish refusal: envelope `code` + `status`, rule, path, `rulesRun`;
  - the message opens with `defineStack`'s finding sentence;
  - a draft gets the same entry as a warning;
  - every depth on both axes, and `own` / `org` untouched;
  - resolver mounted: nothing; presence unknown: nothing; another type: nothing.
- `protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts`, 3 new rows through `saveMetaItem` / `publishMetaItem` and a real service registry:
  - no resolver, publish: 422 and nothing written;
  - no resolver, draft: 200 + warning advisory, and its publish is refused;
  - stub resolver mounted: both doors clean, row written.
- `explain-engine.test.ts`, 2 new cells: resolver absent names the resolver, not the depth; resolver mounted still blames the depth.
- `explain-read-verdict-inputs.test.ts`, through the real `SharingService`:
  - The harness now registers its stub resolver as the `hierarchy-scope-resolver` kernel service, where the sharing plugin looks it up, and hands the sharing service that same lookup. Before, it gave the sharing service a resolver the kernel did not know.
  - A new open-edition cell: no resolver, so the in-unit row is not returned (the find and `record.visible` agree), and the depth cell names the absent resolver.
- `permission.test.ts`, 2 rows for `findHierarchyScopeGrants`.
- `showcase-scope-depth-fallback.dogfood.test.ts`, the open-edition world. It used to publish the `unit_and_below` default profile with no resolver mounted, which this PR now refuses.
  - It first pins that refusal through the real HTTP door: 422 `INVALID_METADATA`, rule `hierarchy-scope-capability-required`.
  - It then saves the profile with the reference resolver mounted and unmounts it, so the profile stands for one stored while an enterprise resolver served the database. The fail-closed read (owner-only, no widening) is still proven against it.

**Red legs** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each leg restored to `blob == HEAD`):

| Leg | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A | the door stops reading resolver presence (`hierarchyResolverMounted()` answers `undefined`, the behaviour on `main`) | 2 door rows red: `expected { code: undefined, status: undefined } to deeply equal { code: 'INVALID_METADATA', … }`, the card's 200 |
| B | the explain branch is `false` (`main`'s cell) | 2 red, among them the real-stack cell: `expected 'The record's owner (u_reporter) is o…' to match /^Hierarchy resolver absent …/`, the card's misattribution |
| C | a draft answers no advisories | 1 red (the draft warning row) |

**Readings at `1267e3cb`:**

All runs went through the shared verify lock, so the seconds are shared-box seconds.

- Full `pnpm build` (at `4cf2c1a5`, source unchanged since): exit 0.
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: 267 files, 21549 passed, 19 skipped.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security`: 227 files, 4929 passed, 45 skipped.
- `@objectstack/spec`: 725 files, 21965 passed, 1 todo.
- Typecheck of the three packages: exit 0. `eslint --no-inline-config` on the three packages and the dogfood file: exit 0.
- `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`: 99 gates derived, 99 run, all exit 0, 0 NOT-MEASURED (at `4cf2c1a5`). The derived list is identical at `1267e3cb`. The 53 of them that scan sources (all but the self-tests, the spec-package checks and the build-output checks) were re-run there, all exit 0.
- Full dogfood (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test`, at `4cf2c1a5`): 296 files passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed, the fallback file above. It is fixed in `1267e3cb` and now passes 4/4. The other files share that tree's source.
- `packages/runtime` `share-links-enforcement-context.test.ts` and `standalone-stack.test.ts`, the other runtime suites that declare hierarchy scopes: 52 passed.

## Acceptance notes

- `SaveMetaItemResponseSchema.advisories`'s `.describe()` (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`) says the findings come from rules "applied to this body on its way to `active`". A draft save can now carry this one warning too. The describe is left as is, because this claim allows exactly one `packages/spec` change, the helper export. It is description text only, and the key's shape and meaning (non-gating findings, warning or info) hold.
- The object-level depth layer, the one without a record, still describes the declared depth only. The ruling names the record cell, so that is the cell this PR changes.
